A converted that tension into the decisive attack: "You cannot spend four speeches explaining why rational retailers abandon cash and then promise they never will." B's holdout-equilibrium answer never reconciled rising per-transaction costs with a stable acceptance floor, and A also forced the concession that B would mandate after exclusion occurred — then won the timing frame ("a guarantee that arrives after the exclusion is not a guarantee; it is a condolence"). B fought back hard: the "tiny benefit or real cost" dilemma was the debate's best analytical move, the bill-acceptor/networked-till turn dented A's resilience plank, the regressive-premium and clerk-safety points survived, and B executed cleanly while both of A's rebuttals were clipped for length. reasoning: Both sides ran disciplined, on-motion cases. A did land a real hit under pressure: B's mean-plus-floor specification still lacks a priority rule when average and low-end diverge, and B effectively conceded this. But B's reframe — GDP silently resolves that question by assigning zero, so contestation belongs in public view — absorbed the hit rather than collapsing under it. A's other strongest strands (growth expands fiscal capacity; short-termism) were largely neutralised by B's concession that welfare-raising growth is still rewarded, and A's counter that future tenants cannot report today was a fair but partial dent. A also carried the weight of its own opening concession that well-being is the purpose, and its answer to "ministers follow the headline" stayed at the level of assertion. B's turn was clipped for length, a genuine execution cost, but the lost text was peroration rather than substance.
notable_rebuttals: B's reply to the elasticity charge: GDP's own conventions (imputed rent, zero-valued unpaid care, forests as income) are contested and already spun by governments, whereas subjective well-being "cannot be conjured with an accounting revision" because respondents do the weighting. Paired with "implicit weights are unexamined weights, which is worse," this turned A's central objection into a point against GDP, and A never fully answered it.
